content:
After a long developer and public beta period, Apple has officially released macOS 26.6 to all users with compatible Macs. Here are the details of this update.

macOS 26.6 is now officially available

macOS 26.6 has been officially released. In addition to fixing over 150 security vulnerabilities, it also includes other bug fixes and performance improvements. These include fixing an issue where some Intel-only apps incorrectly displayed deactivation notifications, as well as bugs affecting HDR screenshots, HealthKit, and Messages.

For users planning to upgrade to macOS 27 Golden Gate later, it is understood that macOS 26.6 will begin an indexing process to support the new Siri AI, the new Siri App, and other features related to the new Apple Intelligence.

Apple has so far only confirmed that this process will be present in iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6, but Mac users appear to be receiving the same arrangement. As users currently testing the macOS 27 Beta will know, the indexing process takes several days, so starting now should help shorten the waiting time after upgrading later.

The official build number of macOS 26.6 is 25G72, which differs from last week's RC build (25G70).

Have you found anything new in macOS 26.6? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
